summary: All 67 records belong to shaving ḥlq 1, not throwing ḥlq 2. The Arabic loan is integrated into I Preterit agent suffixes, Infectum person/object chains and Imperativ. This is a lexical loan verb, not a light-verb construction.

Patient coding alternates explicit hair/beard, a whole person NP, person suffix and objectless self-grooming; none alone requires a new lexical sense. Actor -li in ḥləqli (10/10) differs from patient -li in ḥolaqli.

The source entry explicitly places ḥloqo in Detransitive Infinitiv. Keep this inherited structure, while recognising that event-noun agentivity does not establish a Detransitive finite paradigm. The Detransitive sense list is made explicit for the new result form.
ḥleqa may be a feminine lexical activity noun rather than an inflectional variant of ḥloqo. Its repeated occupation contexts are documented without inventing finite Detransitive forms.
The ḥləqto/dlo ḥloqo contrast recurs in an urgency formula across four texts; one box example and one separately sourced idiom example suffice. Other formula repetitions are checked but not added.
Transcription repairs in MAC NI Sultan and barber/19,21 preserve shifts between me/him and I/you; these are not new senses.

The Jan barber interview adds rich person and patient coding: agent -qe (< -le after q) in ḥləqqe contrasts with patient endings in ḥulaqnowolle and ḥəlqatwolən. The reader's description of -qe as both agent and object at Jan 2.4/513 is not adopted.

Round 1 already provides five active Preterit and Infectum examples, four Imperativ examples, and five inherited-plus-added Infinitiv examples. Only the three-example Infectum-wa cell is filled here, to five.
ḥləqto under ʕal with a price question is an event noun in Jan 2.5/1324, not automatically the agreeing result form from round 1. The similar spelling does not license a new Part. Pass. example.
The women's self-grooming question at Jan 2.5/1334 permits a service interpretation, but the Turoyo alone does not establish a separate causative or get-one's-hair-cut construction.
Does MAC YT LIFE STORY/53 d̥ḥəlaqwo have the customer or an implicit barber as subject? The proposed separate get-one’s-hair-cut construction is not accepted without this distinction.
Should feminine ḥleqa be treated as a separate lexical noun, rather than grouped with the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv ḥloqo?
Verify ḥləqto vocalism and the understood half-face agreement in the urgency formula; preserve the printed vowel.
Does the PrS 15/31 hair command correspond to inherited prs 31/25 by a text/page concordance? The edition mapping is not supplied, so no citation replacement is made.
Confirm the person/object contraction in MAC NI Sultan and barber/21 kḥolaqne; the surrounding quotation is repaired.
Are ḥloqaṯṯe (Jan 2.5/1318), feminine ḥləqto (1324) and ḥleqa different nominal formations? Should they share the inherited Infinitiv heading?
Confirm the segmentation of ḥləqqe qarʕayna (Jan 2.4/513): the -qe is a plural agent ending; the object is the overt possessed head noun.
What body part does harke indicate in Jan 2.12/3087? No example is selected from the gesture-dependent description.
At Jan 2.5/1334 does hair-cutting by the officers' wives refer to their own action or receiving a barber service? No additional lexical sense is inferred.
Heads, sawko and foṯo confirm round 1's broadened hair-cutting/shaving gloss. Human customers, overt hair/face objects and omitted objects remain one sense.
ḥloqo appears with possession, payment, equipment and temporal b-. These nominal environments corroborate the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv filing without proving a finite Detransitive paradigm.
